## At a glance

| | |
|---|---|
| **Input** | A vial of larvae (20 per vial) **or** a resuspended symbiont fraction from an airbrushed homogenate |
| **Output** | Symbiont cells per larva, or cells per cm² of coral surface |
| **Time** | ~10 min per sample for 6 replicate counts (estimate) |
| **Tested on** | *Porites astreoides* larvae; *Galaxea fascicularis* homogenates |

## Materials

- Compound microscope (10× objective)
- Hemocytometer with its coverslip
- Glass Pasteur pipettes
- 0.2 µm filtered seawater (FSW)
- Pestles (larvae) or a homogenizer
- Kimwipes only for cleaning (anything else scratches the hemocytometer)

## Before you start

You need a normalization value for every sample:

- **Larvae:** the number of larvae in the vial.
- **Adult tissue:** the total homogenate volume (recorded when airbrushing) **and** the skeleton surface area.

## Procedure

### A. Sample preparation

**Larvae (20 per vial)**

1. Check the vial number against the master spreadsheet.
2. Homogenize the larvae in the vial with a pestle and **50 µL FSW**.
3. Add **250 µL FSW** while rinsing the pestle into the vial, for **300 µL total**. Record the exact volume.
4. If you also need protein from the same larvae, move **200 µL** to a new vial labeled `<vial#>-P` and freeze it at −80 °C (see [Total protein](total-protein-bca.qmd)).

**Adult homogenates**

5. Use the symbiont fraction resuspended in a known volume of PBS (tube **A-Sym-2** in [Coral tissue removal and homogenization](coral-tissue-removal-homogenization.qmd)). Vortex well before loading.

### B. Load the hemocytometer

6. Put the coverslip over the center of the hemocytometer.
7. With a glass Pasteur pipette, put a small drop at the notch and let capillary action pull it under the coverslip. **Load the same way every time**: uneven loading is the main source of variation.
8. Place it on the microscope stage at 10×.

### C. Count

9. Count all symbiont cells in the **9 large squares** (the 3 × 3 grid bounded by triple lines). Cells touching the boundary lines count as inside.
   - Symbiont cells are round with no ridges, golden-brown to green, and refractile.
10. All 9 squares together are **one replicate**. Count the other chamber for a second replicate.
11. Mix the sample by pipetting between loads and repeat until you have **6 replicate counts**.

### D. Calculate

For a standard improved Neubauer hemocytometer, each large square holds 0.1 µL, so the 9 squares hold 0.9 µL. (TODO: confirm the model of hemocytometer used; the grid volume differs between models.)

$$
\text{cells mL}^{-1} = \frac{\overline{\text{count}}_{9\ \text{squares}}}{9} \times 10^{4}
$$

- **Per larva:** cells mL⁻¹ × sample volume (mL) ÷ number of larvae
- **Per area:** cells mL⁻¹ × total homogenate volume (mL) ÷ surface area (cm²). Account for any dilution, e.g. if the pellet was resuspended in a different volume than it came from.

### Clean-up

- Wipe the hemocytometer and coverslip with a Kimwipe only.
- Rinse pipettes with DI water between samples and before storage. Return the hemocytometer to its case.

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Likely cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| Replicates vary a lot | Uneven loading or cells settling | Load the same volume the same way each time; pipette-mix before every load |
| Too many cells to count | Sample too concentrated | Dilute 1:2 or 1:5 in FSW and multiply back |
| Hard to tell symbionts from debris | Host tissue fragments | Use the washed symbiont pellet (Part C of the tissue protocol) |
